analyst_view.overall: Early view: Leeds are ninth under Farke after beating Tottenham 1-0, while Coventry, 17th under Frank Lampard, lost 3-1 at Everton and are missing Haji Wright, Aurele Amenda, Josh Eccles and Luke Woolfenden. Both play on 21 November first, so this view will be refreshed.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. I lean slightly lower: Leeds' last two league games ended 1-0 and 0-2, and Coventry's attack is weaker without Wright. A narrow home win fits the site's 1.6 to 0.9 split.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.4 corners, which looks low. I lean higher: Leeds should have long spells on the ball at Elland Road, and with wide players such as Gudmundsson and James they should win more than five corners.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.8 cards. Leeds had two bookings against Spurs and Coventry one at Everton, which matches a low figure, so I keep the site's number.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.7 shots, 17.9 of them Leeds'. I lean lower: Leeds needed until the 79th minute to score against Spurs, and with Calvert-Lewin's foot problem their attack lacks a regular focal point, so 18 home shots looks generous.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.7 shots on target. That looks about right for a Leeds side winning narrowly and a Coventry team without its main striker, so I stay with the site.
